land.text: the Badd highlands of Azerbaijan, "southward to near Ardabil and Marand, eastward to the Caspian Sea" and north to the Muqan steppe and the Aras bank

predecessors.note: me-08-a's Abbasid dossier loses "Armenia and Azerbaijan" to the Khurramites in 825 from a Cliopatria shape; the pages opened here show a smaller zone in the Badd highlands.

land.text: Badd Fort and the highlands, taken by Afshin in 837

capitals.name: Badd (Babak Castle, near Kaleybar)
capitals.note: "Babak Castle on Badd, an inaccessible mountain stronghold"; coordinates approximate. The Khurramites page puts it near the Aras River.

rulers.name: Babak Khorramdin
rulers.note: executed at Samira, 14 March 838 (Khurramites page) or probably 7 January 838 (Babak page)

correction.text: Babak's Azerbaijan: Badd, the Marand and Jolfa districts, Nakhchivan and the Muqan steppe

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Khurramite row): Arab historians give Babak's influence "southward to near Ardabil and Marand, eastward to the Caspian Sea", north to the Muqan steppe and the Aras bank, west to the Jolfa, Nakhchivan and Marand districts. The pages give no area; the shape is the researcher's reading of that perimeter (circles at Badd, Marand and Muqan plus Nakhchivan), a rebel zone to be hatched, not a state.

ledger.note: 816: the Khurramites rise under Babak. Al-Tabari records that Babak began his revolt in 816-817; the page says the Khurramites 'began making attacks on Muslim forces in 816'. The land is Azerbaijan around Badd (Babak page).

819: the caliphate sends its first army. 'Caliph al-Ma'mun sent General Yahya ibn Mu'adh against Babak, who won several engagements' (819-820); Isa ibn Muhammad was beaten c. 821-822, Ahmad ibn al-Junayd captured in 824-825 and Muhammad ibn Humayd defeated at Hashtadsar in 829.

837: Afshin takes Badd. 'The last battle between the caliphate and the Khurramites took place at Badd Fort. The Khurramites lost, and Afshin took the fort.' (Babak page: the capture of Babak Castle in 837-838.)
837: the highlands return to the caliphate. Afshin took Badd Fort; Babak fled toward the Aras. me-08-a's Abbasid dossier has Azerbaijan returning in 837.

region.text: the end of the Khurramite revolt

ledger.note: 838: Babak is executed at Samira after Sahl ibn Sumbat hands him over: 'Babak's former ally Sahl ibn Sumbat handed him over' (14 March 838 on this page; probably 7 January 838 on the Babak page). Many thousands of Khurramites fled to Byzantium.

wars.name: Abbasid campaigns against Babak
wars.outcome: Yahya ibn Mu'adh (819-820), Isa ibn Muhammad (c. 821-822), Ahmad ibn al-Junayd (824-825) and Muhammad ibn Humayd (827-829, beaten at Hashtadsar on 9 June 829) failed; in 835 al-Mu'tasim sent Afshin, who took Badd Fort in 837; Babak was handed over by Sahl ibn Sumbat and executed in 838.
wars.note: The Babak page dates Hashtadsar 9 June 829 and calls the capture of the castle 837-838.

wars.name: Khurramite rising around Hamadan
wars.outcome: After al-Ma'mun's death men from Jibal, Hamadan and Isfahan joined the movement and settled near Hamadan; the new army under Ishaq ibn Ibrahim defeated them (60,000 killed per al-Tabari). No land was held.

certainty.note: A mountain redoubt: the extent comes from Arab historians' loose bounds (near Ardabil, Marand, the Aras, the Muqan steppe, the Caspian).

sources.title: Khurramites
sources.note: Dated campaigns 816-838, extent of Babak's influence, Badd Fort 837, execution 14 March 838.

sources.title: Babak Khorramdin
sources.note: Start 816-817, Babak Castle, extent, 829 Hashtadsar, 837-838 capture, execution January 838.

notes: Cliopatria has no Khurramite row (its Shirvan row 825-839 and the Abbasid shape absence in Azerbaijan 825-839 are what me-08-a read as the revolt: the Abbasid dossier loses 'Armenia and Azerbaijan' in 825 and regains them in 837). The pages opened give a much smaller zone than that shape (the Badd highlands, the Marand and Jolfa districts, Nakhchivan, the Muqan steppe) and do not say the Khurramites held Armenia or Arran; the shape here is the researcher's reading of an Arab-historians' perimeter. Wikidata id not known; left null. Disagreements: Babak's execution 14 March 838 (Khurramites page) vs 'probably 7 January 838' (Babak page); the stronghold fell 837 (Khurramites) vs 837-838 (Babak). 'Khurramites' in Tabaristan, Khorasan, Isfahan, Hamadan, Armenia and Basra are named without territorial control and are not drawn; the Babak-Maziyar oath against the Arabs is undated. Counterparts needing a check: the Abbasid dossier's 825 loss region is wider than this one.
